item.title: Thesis submitted at ÉTS
item.description: I submitted my master’s thesis at ÉTS. The work is real-time simulation of surface wear, at the meeting point of physical simulation, contact, and graphics rendering. Version française.

item.title: Master's thesis — contact–appearance coupling for wear in texture space
item.description: Couplage contact-apparence pour l’usure de surfaces microstructurées en simulation interactive — my ÉTS master’s thesis (English abstract title: Visual Appearance Evolution from Wear on Microstructured Surfaces in Texture Space). Directed by Sheldon Andrews, defended 14 August 2026. The core idea: give material maps a persistent local memory of contact. Body travel alone cannot predict where wear shows up. Version française.

item.title: CAÉC 2026 poster, second place in Optics
item.description: I presented a poster at CAÉC 2026, the annual congress of student researchers, on real-time simulation of visual texture wear fed by experimental data. I placed second in the Optics category. Version française.

item.title: AlgoÉTS MarkÉTS — first ÉTS paper-trading competition
item.description: While I was president of AlgoÉTS, the club ran its first campus-wide paper-trading competition on MarkÉTS. The numbers below come from the club summary featured on my LinkedIn profile. Version française.

item.title: GraphQuon 2025 — University of Toronto
item.description: GraphQuon is the annual Quebec–Ontario pre-SIGGRAPH workshop. The 2025 edition ran 15–16 November 2025 at the University of Toronto (series page). I presented there with Sheldon Andrews (ÉTS): Where to Wear? — how frictional contact leaves a readable history on surfaces, and how we can turn that into graphics and engineering feedback. Version française.

item.title: GraphQuon 2024 — ÉTS (Montréal)
item.description: GraphQuon (formerly MOTOGRAPH) is the annual Quebec–Ontario pre-SIGGRAPH workshop for East-Canadian computer graphics labs. The 2024 edition ran 9–10 November 2024 at École de technologie supérieure (ÉTS) in Montréal. I helped build and host the conference website at graphquon.github.io so schedules, registration, and past editions stayed in one place. Version française.
